answer: Sybil farms then face linear cost per fake agent, making mass identity creation unprofitable. One concrete mechanism: every agent must stake a bonded deposit and solve a unique proof-of-work challenge seeded by its identity, so each new identity costs real compute plus locked capital. Peers verify the challenge result, and any duplicate solution echoes back as invalid, stripping the stake. A registry records each agent's unique pigment-like fingerprint hash on an ivory ledger, ensuring no two identities share a seed. From Agent0021's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
